title: A password change is told to the account's address
assertion: A completed reset writes one pending notice in its own transaction, by the database, only for the account's own `password_reset_completed` (the actor a person and the object that person), and a refused, invalid or rolled-back reset, the invitation's first password or any other action none; a confirmation made while the database cannot be reached fails at the account's lookup, before the provider is asked, so the password is unchanged; a completed reset whose sessions could not be ended queues none and its line pages the operator (`PasswordResetSessionsNotEnded`); the platform job sends one message on the transactional stream (kind `password_changed`, subject the notice, recipient the user) to the account's address, once however many runs race, read only by the claim of a pending, due notice under 24 hours old, with the change's time in UTC, the four lines, the second naming the second factor only to an account the claim returns as enrolled and ending at the sessions for one that is not, the support route, Reply-To the support address, the account footer in both alternatives and no link, from MailFromAddress through the operator role's transactional statement alone, and records `password_notice_sent`; it retries after 1, 5, 15 and 60 minutes, counts a record that fails after SES accepted the message as a try (`RecordFailed`), fails at the fifth try or at once on a permanent error, stops claiming once a run has spent 8 seconds sending, and fails a notice not sent within 24 hours as `NoticeStale`; a bounce, suppression or rejection of its own `password_changed` message, recorded before or after the send, makes it undelivered, reported once (`password_notice_undelivered`, and `PASSWORD_NOTICE_UNDELIVERED` by IDs, logged before the event leaves the queue, which pages), a complaint changes nothing, and the end state is the same in any order of the send and its events, concurrent ones included; no payload, log or error holds the address; the reset is never blocked or undone by the notice, and a provider sign-out that fails still sends the same lines and pages the operator (`PasswordResetProviderSignOutFailed`); the two cases this row first recorded as open (a step that proved the old password before a reset opening a session when its code is answered after it, and a key-registration step begun before a reset registering a key after it when the provider's sign-out had no effect) are closed by SGN-17, where they are asserted refused
noFileReason: The notices are queued and sent against a synthetic database, to an in-memory sender or the local outbox; no file.
